Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Absolutive is unmarked (-Ø) in Matis. Both S and O bear no case marker. Ergative A is marked with -n.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: Matis 1st person singular pronouns follow ergative alignment: A=embi, S/O=ebi. The 1+2 inclusive nuki/muki is neutral (invariant).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Matis 2nd person singular follows ergative alignment (A=mimbi, S/O=mibi), but 2nd person plural follows ACCUSATIVE alignment: mikui in A/S position, mitso in O position. So there is a singular/plural split: singular=ergative, plural=accusative.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: Matis 3rd person singular non-emphatic is Ø (neutral). 3rd person plural non-emphatic: Ø in A/S, ato in O — accusative alignment. 4th person (emphatic/coreferential): akui in A/S, ato in O — accusative alignment. Overall, 3rd person pronouns do NOT follow ergative alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs in Matis follow strict ergative-absolutive case marking: A marked with -n (ERG), S and O unmarked (-Ø, ABS). See ex. (1a,b): dëndu-n 'electric.eel-ERG', tumi-Ø 'man's.name-ABS'.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: No aspect-based split documented. Fleck explicitly states: 'there are no typical split alignment systems in Mayoruna languages, such as splits conditioned by tense/aspect/mood' (p. 35). Ergative alignment applies regardless of aspect.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: No aspect-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in perfective contexts. Ex. (1a) uses immediate past inflection with ergative A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in past tense. Ex. (1a): dëndu-n tumi-Ø pëdka-a-sh 'electric.eel-ERG man's.name-ABS shock-IMM.PAST-3'.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-past. Ex. (25a): ëmbi du-Ø pe-e-k '1ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-NPAST-INDIC'.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in indicative mood.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-indicative moods.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in realis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in irrealis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: No agentivity-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with agentive A. Extended intransitive verbs (§4) are an exception at the verb-class level, not agentivity-based.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Psych-verbs and experiencer verbs in Matis are treated as transitive with the Experiencer in ergative case (p. 48). E.g. dais 'desire, covet' takes ERG Experiencer. Ergative applies with non-agentive A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: No animacy-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with animate A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No animacy-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with inanimate A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Ergative alignment is documented in main clauses. This is the primary context described.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Ergative alignment has been extended to reanalyzed negative constructions (§6.1) AND abilitative constructions (§6.2) in Matis. Ex. (25b): ëmbi du-Ø pe-emen(-pa) ik-e-k '1ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-NEG AUX-NPAST-INDIC'. Ex. (31b): dabi-n du-Ø pe-tepad 'David-ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-ABIL'. Matis is further along in ergativizing these constructions than Matses.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Yes, two conditioning factors: (1) VERB CLASS: extended intransitive verbs (bëama 'forget', cho 'have') take two ABS arguments. (2) NOMINAL CLASS/NUMBER: singular pronouns (1sg, 2sg, 3sg emphatic) are ergative; 1+2 inclusive nuki/muki is neutral; 2pl and 3pl pronouns follow ACCUSATIVE alignment (mikui/miki in A/S, mitso in O; akui in A/S, ato in O). This is a three-way ergative-neutral-accusative split in the pronoun system.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Yes. On full nouns, ergative case is marked identically to genitive and instrumental: -n (with allomorph -ën after consonants). Note: on pronouns, ergative and genitive differ in form (e.g. 1sg ERG=embi, GEN=nukun).

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Yes for instrumental: on full nouns, ergative and instrumental are both marked with -n. Comitative is expressed by a distinct postposition: -bëd 'Comitative' (p. 37). So: ergative = instrumental (same marker -n), but ergative ≠ comitative.
